lessons.title: Trauma-Informed Care and the Patient as Partner
lessons.topicSummary: Formal introduction of the guest endometriosis surgeon, her philosophy of the physician-patient relationship as a team (clinician brings medical/surgical expertise; the patient is the expert in their own values, goals, and lived experience), and why medical trauma disproportionately affects women and vulnerable populations.

lessons.title: Medical Gaslighting, Diagnostic Delay, and Patient Fatigue
lessons.topicSummary: Gaslighting as a primary driver of medical trauma in endometriosis; how dismissal (e.g., 'manage your anxiety') causes diagnostic delay; the 'self-gaslighting' that makes patients doubt their own symptoms; blame and lack of validation compounding into an exponential delay in care and patient fatigue.

lessons.title: The Neurobiology of Trauma and Trauma-Informed Accommodations
lessons.topicSummary: The association between severe childhood trauma and endometriosis risk; chronic HPA-axis activation and sympathetic overdrive in neuroinflammatory conditions; meeting patients where they are with individualized accommodations (nitrous, sedation, anesthesia for sensitive exams); and challenging the paternalistic practice of basing transvaginal ultrasound on sexual history rather than patient comfort.

lessons.title: Patient Empowerment, Subspecialty Care, and Educating the Profession
lessons.topicSummary: Counseling patients with full disclosure of all options to empower their choices; the necessity of subspecialty care given co-occurring conditions (adenomyosis overlaps in up to 80% of cases, pelvic floor dysfunction, EDS, POTS); and educating students and colleagues that painful periods are not normal and warrant evaluation.

lessons.title: The Future of Women's Health: Subspecialization and the OB/GYN Debate
lessons.topicSummary: The debate over separating obstetrics from gynecology; how subspecialties arose as a 'pressure release valve' when four years could not train competency across all areas; the tension between urban specialization and rural healthcare deserts; and the historical, patriarchal origins of OB/GYN unification.

lessons.title: Provider Burnout, Emotional Regulation, and Recovery as a Fresh Start
lessons.topicSummary: The emotional toll on physicians and the case for emotional-regulation training; how a system that teaches suppression perpetuates harm; screening patients for support systems; framing surgery as a fresh start rather than a quick fix (recovery can rival major life stressors); and a structured post-operative care process with continued learning from patient advocates.

lessons.title: The Neuroimmune Model of Endometriosis
lessons.topicSummary: The cell danger response and vagus-nerve link to inflammation; vagus-nerve stimulation research; the parasympathetic 'rest, digest, heal' state versus persistent fight-or-flight and autoimmunity; endometriosis as a possible neuroimmune activation ('period flu'); nutrient depletion and systemic functional-medicine approaches; and reproductive immunology with immune-system sex differences.

lessons.title: Emerging and Adjunct Therapies
lessons.topicSummary: Emerging and adjunct therapies discussed for endometriosis and co-occurring conditions: GLP-1 medications with cautions about muscle-mass loss, low-dose naltrexone, and mast-cell activation management, framed as options to explore with full patient disclosure.
